findings: The Dutch-taught Utrecht Information Science bachelor totals 180 EC. Appendix D records ten 7.5 EC compulsory courses, an individual 15 EC research project, four 7.5 EC modules from one complete path, and two more 7.5 EC major electives. The 45 EC of profiling is open with the intermediate/advanced-level and non-overlap conditions. The example retains Information Systems as the general extension of the compulsory organisational and systems work, independent of UCR fit. The first eligible electives outside that path are Cognition and Emotion and Usability Engineering and User Experience. The three advanced path courses, advanced UX elective and advanced research project total 45 EC at level 3. Two compulsory tutorial activities carry no credits; old equivalent listings add no credits.

The eight first-year courses supply 60 EC including Scientific Research Methods. In the published teaching cycle, a Year 2 illustration pairs Architecture of Digital Ecosystems (B) and Academic Skills (D) in period 1, with Systems Development Methods in period 2, Information Security in period 3 and Strategic Management in period 4, using the remaining places for profiling courses. After these first 120 EC, a Year 3 illustration can take Usability Engineering in period 1, Product Software (C) alongside Cognition and Emotion (A) in period 2, and the individual research project full-time in an available period, with remaining places for profiling. Moving Cognition and Emotion to Year 3 avoids its period-2 slot clash with Systems Development Methods. The student guide permits the research project across two periods at half time or one at full time and requires 120 EC and prior Scientific Research Methods. This illustrates the progression with 2026 slots, subject to later timetables and eligible non-overlapping profiling choices.

The closest option adds practical software development after the programming gateway. The data option keeps its full quantitative sequence. The human option now uses empirical evidence synthesis after experimental methods; the remaining curriculum preserves perception, cognition and social behaviour. The audience explanation separates UX and security gaps and the required research project from optional UCR independent research.
